question: P is the mid-point of side BC of a parallelogram ABCD such that ∠BAP = ∠DAP. If AD = 10 cm, then CD = ?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

In a **parallelogram**, if the **angle bisector** of one angle meets the midpoint of the opposite side, the triangle formed is always **isosceles**.

Here, **AP** is the bisector of ∠**A** and **P** is the midpoint of **BC**.

Since **AD || BC**, the alternate interior angle ∠**BPA** = ∠**DAP**.

Thus, in Δ**ABP**, ∠**BAP** = ∠**BPA**, making **AB = BP**.

Since **BP = BC/2 = AD/2**, we get **AB = 10/2 = 5 cm**.

Opposite sides are equal: **CD = AB = 5 cm**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:** **ABCD** is a **parallelogram**, **P** is the midpoint of **BC**, ∠**BAP** = ∠**DAP**, and **AD** = 10 cm.

**Formula Used:** In a **parallelogram**, opposite sides are parallel and equal. Base angles of an **isosceles triangle** are equal.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c61b2ba33b6500bd6bfd27f5cf9fecd918a69bad53d1359101f4dfbac87f4c3b.png] 

⇒ In **parallelogram ABCD**, **AD = BC = 10 cm** (Opposite sides are equal).

⇒ **P** is the midpoint of **BC**, ∴ **BP = PC = 10 ÷ 2 = 5 cm**.

⇒ Since **AD || BC** and **AP** is a transversal, ∠**DAP = ∠BPA** (Alternate interior angles).

⇒ Given ∠**BAP = ∠DAP**, ∴ ∠**BAP = ∠BPA**.

⇒ In Δ**ABP**, sides opposite to equal angles are equal, ∴ **AB = BP**.

⇒ **AB = 5 cm**.

⇒ In **parallelogram ABCD**, **CD = AB** (Opposite sides are equal).

⇒ **CD = 5 cm**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 cm.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Properties of a Parallelogram

Opposite sides are parallel and equal (**AB = CD**, **BC = AD**). Adjacent angles are supplementary (sum = 180°).

Alternate Interior Angles

When two parallel lines are cut by a transversal, the pairs of angles on opposite sides of the transversal and between the parallel lines are equal.

Isosceles Triangle Property

If two angles of a triangle are equal, the sides opposite to those angles are also equal (Converse of Isosceles Triangle Theorem).</p
